changes: Pointer null checks identified by Rust diagnostic items use value-only contexts. Their bodies are still checked.
Unknown writes do not change immutable static storage when its type has no interior mutability.
The same read-only rule is used for serial reads, parallel reads and opaque-call writes.
Mutable statics and storage with interior mutability remain exposed to unknown writes. References from read-only storage are still followed.
The measurement result now includes the scenario process peak commit separately from dependency compiler peaks.
limits: No memory limit. No time limit.

kernel_like_baseline.verdict: The old checker also rejected unresolved IRQ calls. Both runs report the same set of diagnostic source locations; diagnostic counts differ.

source_changes: The scenario sources and features are unchanged from the recorded baseline cases.

existing_scenario_checks.result: All six safe cases were accepted. All six negative cases were rejected for the expected forbidden call. The runner also checked the saved call graph.

runs.verdict: Rejected: unresolved IRQ call paths. This is not a successful policy check.

notes: A fast compile can finish between private-memory samples. Use the process peak commit counter for the fast cases, not their sampled private value alone.
The kernel-like case still has a substantial formatting and iteration cost. This change does not remove all context growth.
The actual rustOS kernel has not been checked with this build.
